slides.title:
Guest Wi-Fi is a
*security posture*,
not an amenity.
slides.body: It rarely gets designed that way.

slides.title: What gets designed
slides.body:
The splash page.
Logo, terms checkbox,
maybe an email capture.

slides.title: The problem
slides.body:
That's the *least* interesting
decision in it.
And the only one reviewed.

slides.title: What can it reach?
slides.body:
The internet, plus three
things somebody
*needed once*.

slides.title: The three
steps: A file share that was supposed to be *temporary*.

slides.title: What can it resolve?
slides.body:
A guest VLAN on the
internal resolver enumerates
the estate from the *parking lot*.

slides.title:
How long does a
device stay on it?
slides.body:
A lease measured in days
isn't a guest network.
It's an unmanaged corporate one.

slides.title: When it's abused
slides.body:
Can you name
the *device*?
Does anyone own the answer?

slides.title: Not more friction
slides.body:
A harder portal just pushes
people onto a *hotspot*.
Worse for everyone.

slides.title:
The one network you
*intend* strangers to use.
slides.body:
It should be the one
you can describe
most precisely.

Follow *@mzsnetworks*
